title: Evaluating Implementation Effectiveness in Malaysian Higher TVET: A Lean Waste–SERVQUAL Integrated Framework
content:
The goal of this research is to analyze an application of the Lean Waste-SERVQUAL framework for Malaysian Higher Technical Vocational Education and Training (TVET) using PLS-SEM. The results suggest that lean waste reduction is a significant predictor of successful implementation and that SERVQUAL serves to complement lean waste by providing a sustainable perspective through which to evaluate service quality, confidence among stakeholders, and institutional improvement efforts.


ABSTRACT

Malaysia's technical and vocational education and training (TVET) system aims to deliver hands-on skills that produce highly qualified workers who are proficient in Industry 4.0. However, there are ongoing operational inefficiencies and service quality gaps across many higher TVET institutions, which have limited their overall performance despite numerous policy changes. This study evaluates the effectiveness characteristics of the existing Malaysian higher TVET system using a combined framework of lean waste reduction and SERVQUAL models. A quantitative approach involving 30 respondents from selected Malaysian higher TVET institutions was analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). Through correlation and structural equation modelling analyses, lean waste reduction was found to have an indefinitely positive impact on perceived operational performance. In contrast, the SERVQUAL dimensions did not significantly affect the implementation outcome; they remain conceptually important for developing a sustainable, vocational institutions framework. Evidence shows that employing a quality improvement framework which has operational efficiency and stakeholder satisfaction leads to these desirable outcomes. The current research adds to the empirical literature and provides useful contextual information for policymakers and institutional leaders interested in improving the performance and sustainability of Malaysia's higher TVET. Future research could use a larger sample or longitudinal research methods.
